articles.content: Business News India WATCH: First glimpse of how India's first indigenous bullet train is being built WATCH: First glimpse of how India's first indigenous bullet train is being built The indigenous B28 trainset, being manufactured by Integral Coach Factory and BEML, is designed for a speed of 280 kmph, with track trials expected by mid-2027 Advertisement Share: India's first indigenous bullet train is being built at ICF, BEML Business Today Desk Nov 1, 2026, Updated Nov 1, 2026 6:33 PM IST Subscribe to Notifications Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Sunday shared a glimpse of India's first indigenously designed bullet train taking shape at BEML's manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. Vaishnaw inspected the manufacturing unit and witnessed a squeeze test being conducted on the train's structure. The indigenous B28 trainset, being manufactured by Integral Coach Factory (ICF) and BEML, is designed for a speed of 280 kmph, with track trials expected by mid-2027. Advertisement Read More Read More | B28 trainset designed for 280 kmph: Ashwini Vaishnaw reveals the engineering behind India's first bullet train Explaining the different components of the train during his inspection, Vaishnaw said, "The first bullet train we have designed as per international standards. This is the roof wall, this is the side, these are the side walls, and that is the cab. And those are the end walls." "So, the entire structure is designed as per international standards, and it is undergoing the most rigorous squeeze test because when the train runs at those very high speeds, then around the train, a vacuum gets created," he added. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal also shared a separate video showing the manufacturing of the train's side panels. Advertisement B28 to run at 280 kmph, B35 next in line Earlier in October, Vaishnaw had outlined India's indigenous bullet train manufacturing programme, confirming that the first body frame of the B28 was complete and undergoing structural testing. "ICF and BEML are manufacturing the indigenous B28 trainset, designed for 280 kmph. The first body frame is complete and is undergoing structural testing. Track trials are expected by mid-2027. A faster B35, designed for 350 kmph, is the next step," the minister had said. The J-slab ballastless track system, based on Japanese high-speed rail technology, is also being produced at Indian casting yards by Indian engineers for the first time. articles.title: 80% of India's First Bullet Train Project Completed; Surat–Vapi Section Expected to Open in 2027
articles.content: New Delhi, 01 November (H.S.): India is set to usher in a new era of high-speed rail travel, with the country’s first bullet train project making significant progress. Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has shared a promotional video offering a glimpse of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project, which is currently under construction. The 11-second video features messages such as ‘Coming Soon’, ‘Construction of India’s First Bullet Train’ and ‘Stay Tuned’, along with a preview of the train’s interior. Nearly 80 per cent of the ambitious project has been completed. Spanning 508 kilometres, the Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor is witnessing rapid progress in the construction of bridges, tunnels and track infrastructure. The first operational section, between Surat and Vapi, is expected to open in August 2027. Once fully operational, the bullet train will cover the distance between Mumbai and Ahmedabad in approximately one hour and 58 minutes. A total of 12 stations are planned along the corridor. The trains will have a design speed of 350 kmph and an operational speed of 320 kmph, considerably higher than the 180 kmph design speed of India's existing Vande Bharat trains. The project will incorporate world-class safety standards, advanced signalling systems and sophisticated train control technologies. The MAHSR project is not limited to a single route but is laying a strong foundation for India's future high-speed rail network. A standardised template is being developed on the basis of this project for upcoming bullet train corridors across the country. The Central Government is planning to expand the high-speed rail network beyond the Mumbai–Ahmedabad corridor. Seven additional high-speed rail corridors, spanning approximately 4,000 kilometres, have been identified for future development. These strategically selected routes are expected to attract investments of around Rs. 16 lakh crore, potentially making a significant contribution to the country's long-term economic growth. articles.title: Pioxazon, India's First Discovered Insecticide Molecule Brought To Farmers By PI
articles.content: Hyderabad: PI Industries today launched Pioxazon (Pioxaniliprole 20% SC), powered by India’s first indigenously discovered insecticide molecule. Developed for rice, maize and Bengal gram, Pioxazon marks a significant milestone in PI’s journey from original scientific discovery to commercial application. Its molecule, Pioxaniliprole, is a defining moment in India’s agricultural innovation journey. It shows that India can now discover, develop, register and commercialise crop protection innovation of its own, and Pioxazon is the first product to complete that journey. Rice, maize and Bengal gram are among the most important crops in Indian agriculture, and across southern India they form the backbone of farming. Andhra Pradesh is considered as “the rice bowl of India”, Karnataka is its largest maize producer, and Bengal gram is the leading pulse crop grown in Andhra Pradesh. For millions of farming families across the region, protecting these crops means protecting their livelihoods. Indian farmers face evolving pest pressures, erratic weather and rising crop-protection costs. Yellow Stem Borer in rice, Fall Armyworm in maize and Pod Borer in Bengal gram remain significant challenges for farmers. Drawing on PI’s eight decades of engagement with Indian agriculture, Pioxazon has been evaluated through multilocation field trials under diverse growing conditions. It is registered by the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee (CIB&RC) for use against Yellow Stem Borer in rice, Fall Armyworm in maize and Pod Borer in Bengal gram. Commenting on the launch, Mayank Singhal, Vice Chairperson and Managing Director, PI Industries Ltd, said, “Pioxazon marks a defining milestone in PI’s innovation journey. With Pioxaniliprole, we have demonstrated our ability to originate proprietary science and take it through the complete innovation lifecycle, from discovery and development to registration. As Pioxazon reaches farmers, we are taking Indian innovation from discovery to the field, guided by a deep understanding of India’s diverse farming realities. For farmers, it means a solution built for the pests and weather they face today. For PI, it strengthens our ambition to take the best of Indian innovation to the world.” Pioxazon brings together four distinct advantages. It offers the fastest absorption, within 30 minutes of application, delivering excellent rainfastness and the best performance in erratic weather. Its unique molecular structure gives it excellent binding affinity to the pest, delivering the highest efficacy and consistent, robust protection. With maximum availability in the plant system and exceptional translaminar action, it moves quickly through the plant to provide the longest duration of control, along with a phytotonic effect. It is also the safest for beneficial insects, including predatory spiders, predatory beetles, ladybird beetles, damselflies and green lacewings, which help keep pest populations in check naturally. This makes Pioxazon an environmentally conscious choice, well suited to Integrated Pest Management practices. Saket Bhatnagar, CEO – India Brands, PI AgSciences, said, “Farmers judge a crop-protection product by what happens in the field after they spray. Pioxazon has been built to deliver where it matters most: fast action that holds up when the weather turns, and control that lasts. We will take Pioxazon to...

articles.title: Ashwini Vaishnaw inspects India's first bullet train production in Bengaluru - The News Mill
articles.content: ANI Photo | Ashwini Vaishnaw inspects India’s first bullet train production in Bengaluru Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw inspected the manufacturing of India’s first bullet train at BEML in Bengaluru on November 1, expressing satisfaction with the project’s progress and focus on quality and international standards. Speaking after the inspection, Vaishnaw stated, “Today, I conducted a thorough inspection of the bullet train currently being manufactured at BEML. The progress is excellent. All major components of the bullet train are being produced, integrated, and tested; the entire process is advancing very well, with a special emphasis on quality.” ADVERTISEMENT Stay connected Make The News Mill your preferred source See more TNM stories when you search for news on Google. Add TNM on Google He noted the critical importance of managing and sustaining atmospheric pressure due to the vacuum created around the train at high speeds. “Testing is conducted at loads of 1500 kilonewtons. Great attention has been paid to every aspect, and each component has been tested according to international standards,” he added. Earlier on the same day, Vaishnaw flagged off the Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper train, connecting Bengaluru’s Sir M Visvesvaraya Railway Station (SMVT) with Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT). ADVERTISEMENT Commenting on the new service, BJP MP Tejasvi Surya described it as a valuable gift from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the people of Karnataka. He added that the Railway Minister agreed to consider another significant proposal: establishing a high-speed rail corridor connecting Bengaluru to Pune via Hubballi. Surya said, “On this important day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has given a valuable gift to the people of the state: the Vande Bharat Sleeper Train Service connecting Mumbai and Bengaluru. The demand is so high that the train is already fully booked for the next three full weeks. That is the kind of demand that exists between the two cities. The Railway Minister has also agreed to consider positively the other most important demand that all of us have put forward: to connect Bengaluru to Pune via Hubballi through a high-speed rail corridor, through a bullet train corridor.” Written by TNM (With ANI Inputs) This story is written by TNM Bureau with inputs from ANI. articles.title: India's First Bullet Train Takes Shape: Railway Minister Vaishnaw Reviews Manufacturing Progress
articles.content: Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw, today reviewed the manufacturing of Bharat-made Bullet Train-B28, at ADITYA - manufacturing Facility in Bengaluru. The Minister reviewed the specialised manufacturing infrastructure, including precision-engineered jigs and fixtures for carbody fabrication, and witnessed key stages of production such as underframe, sidewall, roof assembly, car assembly, surface preparation, treatment etc. These advanced manufacturing processes are critical to achieving the precision, strength and quality standards required for high-speed rail operations. He also witnessed the ‘Squeeze Test’ demonstration, a critical quality assurance process in which the train carbody is subjected to controlled compressive/tensile forces to assess its structural strength, rigidity and dimensional stability. He examined passenger seats, focusing on the comfort and convenience they will offer during high-speed journeys, and reviewed key onboard systems and components, including the Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) system, couplers and other train equipment and assemblies. He also reviewed side module, roof module manufacturing and witnessed the subsequent integration and assembly operations. articles.title: "Excellent progress": Ashwini Vaishnaw after inspecting manufacturing of India's first bullet ...
articles.content: Bengaluru ( Karnataka ) [India], November 1 (ANI): Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Sunday inspected the manufacturing of India’s first bullet train at BEML in Bengaluru and expressed satisfaction over the progress of the project, highlighting the focus on quality and adherence to international standards. Speaking to ANI after the inspection, the Railway Minister said that all major components of the bullet train were being manufactured, integrated and tested, with the overall process progressing well. “Today, I conducted a thorough inspection of the bullet train currently being manufactured at BEML. The progress is excellent. All major components of the bullet train are being produced, integrated, and tested; the entire process is advancing very well, with a special emphasis on quality,” Vaishnaw said. “Given that a vacuum is created around the train at such high speeds, managing and sustaining atmospheric pressure is critical—testing is conducted at loads of 1500 kilonewtons. Great attention has been paid to every aspect, and each component has been tested according to international standards,” he added. Earlier in the day, Vaishnaw flagged off the Bengaluru - Mumbai Vande Bharat Sleeper train, connecting Bengaluru ’s Sir M Visvesvaraya Railway Station (SMVT) with Mumbai ’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT). Speaking on the occasion, BJP MP Tejasvi Surya described the new service as a valuable gift from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the people of Karnataka . He also said that the Railway Minister had agreed to positively consider another key demand: connecting Bengaluru to Pune via Hubballi through a high-speed rail corridor. "On this important day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has given a valuable gift to the people of the state: the Vande Bharat Sleeper Train Service connecting Mumbai and Bengaluru . The demand is so high that the train is already fully booked for the next three full weeks. That is the kind of demand that exists between the two cities. The Railway Minister has also agreed to consider positively the other most important demand that all of us have put forward: to connect Bengaluru to Pune via Hubballi through a high-speed rail corridor, through a bullet train corridor," he told ANI. articles.title: Chhattisgarh's Khaira becomes India's first 100 per cent solar village under PM Surya Ghar yojana
articles.content: RAIPUR: In the quiet rural contours of Chhattisgarh’s Rajnandgaon district, a small village, Khaira, pulled off a noteworthy milestone. Every single one of its 141 households now gleams with rooftop solar panels, establishing Khaira as India’s first village to achieve 100% saturation under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana , officials said. Home to 889 residents, the village now boasts an aggregate clean energy capacity of nearly 282 kW, with a 2 kW setup mounted atop every home. Even more noteworthy is that the entire transformation cost the villagers nothing. While central and state subsidies covered the baseline, corporate social responsibility (CSR) funding bridged the remaining financial gap, ensuring zero out-of-pocket expenditure for the residents. The gram panchayat gains a new identity. For decades, electricity meant an inescapable monthly expense competing against food, medicine, and household basics. Under the new net-metering framework, that dynamic has been completely flipped. “Khaira’s families have transitioned from passive, grid-dependent consumers into self-reliant urjadatas —energy producers who feed their surplus power back into the utility grid. The shift represents not just lower utility meters, but an empowering psychological pivot where clean technology is no longer an urban luxury, but an integral part of everyday rural domestic life,” Jitendra Yadav, Rajnandgaon collector told this newspaper. “Rooftop solar adoption in India has often skewed toward affluent, urban consumers capable of navigating complex bank loans and heavy paperwork. Khaira reversed this trend by putting vulnerable households first,” averred Bhupendra Yadav, Khaira sarpanch. Out of the 141 electrified homes, 93 belong to beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G), meaning their newly constructed pukka homes came equipped with renewable power right from day one. The village's 21 Scheduled Tribe families (88 individuals) and four Scheduled Caste families (18 individuals) share equally in this clean energy dividend, the collector added. For elderly residents and single providers living on fixed incomes, the relief is apparently profound. Shohgil Gond, a widow living alone on her pension, said, "I live alone and depend only on my pension. Now I don't have to worry about the electricity bill." Kartik Yadav, a PMAY-G beneficiary managing domestic work and manual labor, echoes that relief, "My earnings are small. With solar, I won't have to worry about the electricity bill anymore." Khaira’s solar leap was not won through top-down mandates, but through intimate community trust. The breakthrough was driven by local women mobilizers—known as PM Surya Sakhis —including local champion Sangeeta Sahu, working in tandem with the extensive self-help group network of Padma Shri awardee Phoolbasan Bai Yadav and village sarpanch Yadav. By orchestrating seamless coordination among district administration, rural banking networks, grassroots women leaders, and CSR partners, Khaira has offered a practical roadmap for India’s decentralized energy ambitions. It proves that when clean energy policy meets grassroots trust, the transition toward an Urja Aatmanirbhar (energy self-reliant) nation can start where it matters most—right from the village rooftop.

articles.title: India's First Fusion Power Company Advances Plans For Private Tokamak Reactor
articles.content: If Pranos Fusion achieves its objectives, India could move significantly closer to privately developed fusion energy, with the design of the country's first privately built tokamak reactor expected to be finalised in 2027, The Hindu reported . The Bangalore-based Start-Up has already developed PRAGYA, a compact doughnut-shaped tokamak designed to validate plasma control systems and high-temperature superconducting magnet technologies. The experimental machine is intended to serve as a stepping stone towards PRANIK, a substantially larger fusion reactor capable of generating the extreme temperatures required for nuclear fusion. According to co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Shaurya Kaushal, the company expects to complete the PRANIK blueprint by 2027 and begin progressing towards a practical reactor capable of producing energy. He emphasised, however, that generating commercial electricity from fusion remains a longer-term objective. “By 2027, we expect to finalise the blueprint for PRANIK and be on our way to building a practical reactor that can produce energy. To be able to actually produce electricity from fusion is a further step away.” Pranos Fusion is currently incubated at the Institute of Plasma Research, which operates under the Department of Atomic Energy, as well as the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research in Bangalore, which is supported by the Department of Science and Technology. Unlike conventional nuclear power stations, which rely on fission reactions involving uranium, fusion generates energy when light atomic nuclei combine. Most fusion concepts focus on merging deuterium and tritium, two forms of hydrogen, to produce helium and a high-energy neutron while releasing substantial amounts of energy. Achieving fusion requires temperatures approaching 100 million degrees Celsius, several times hotter than the Sun's core. At such temperatures, matter exists as plasma, making physical containment impossible. Tokamaks overcome this challenge by using powerful magnetic fields to suspend and control the plasma without allowing it to touch reactor walls. Pranos Fusion was among the deep-technology companies highlighted during the Emerging Science Technology and Innovation Conclave held recently. Roshan George, co-founder and a Computer Science engineer from the Manipal Institute of Technology, noted that although fusion-generated electricity remains distant and currently expensive, future demand for clean energy sources is expected to rise substantially. “Electricity from a fusion reactor is still far away and would be expensive now, however the need for any source of energy is only going to grow.” He further highlighted fusion's safety and fuel advantages. “Fusion’s advantage is that while [it’s] nuclear power, it doesn’t need radioactive material like uranium. India already produces plenty of deuterium. Fusion reactions are also not chain reactions, and therefore the risk of a runaway reaction [like in a fission reactor] is almost absent.” Globally, fusion research continues to advance through large-scale international projects. The most prominent is the International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) under construction in southern France. The multinational project includes India, the European Union, the United States, Russia, China, Japan and South Korea. articles.title: Assam signs MoU with Belgian firm's subsidiary for India's first public proton beam therapy unit
articles.content: Guwahati, Oct 31 (PTI) The Assam government on Saturday signed an agreement with the Indian subsidiary of Belgium's Ion Beam Applications SA for setting up the country's first public proton beam therapy centre in the northeastern state, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said. He said this advanced technology will make a significant difference for patients, particularly children, receiving cancer care. "I am extremely proud to share that Assam has signed an MoU to set up India's first proton beam therapy centre in the public health sector at a cost of Rs 600 cr," Sarma said in a social media post. Until now, proton beam therapy, one of the world's most advanced cancer treatments, had been available only in private hospitals in India, at costs of up to Rs 50 lakh, he said. "Assam seeks to change that today. This advanced technology attacks tumours with pinpoint precision while sparing healthy tissues. For suitable patients, particularly children, that can make a significant difference," he added. "With 17 cancer hospitals being set up across the state, of which 12 are functional, a community-level constant outreach programme and consistent investments in human capital and infrastructure, our ambition is clear: Assam will be a global centre for cancer care," Sarma added. Speaking at the MoU signing event here, Sarma termed the initiative an important milestone in the state government's sustained efforts to make advanced cancer treatment accessible to and affordable for ordinary citizens. "Cancer continues to be one of the major public health challenges. Our government firmly believes that access to quality healthcare should not depend on the patients' place of living or their ability to travel to distant cities for treatment. With this commitment, we have been steadily strengthening cancer care infrastructure across Assam. The proton beam therapy centre is another important step in that direction," he said. Highlighting the benefits of the therapy, Sarma said, "Proton therapy can help protect vital organs such as the brain, heart and spine in children undergoing cancer treatment. It can also reduce the risk of certain long-term complications and second cancers later in life. This is an important consideration when we are treating young patients." The chief minister said that of the approximate investment of Rs 600 crore in the project, World Bank will provide Rs 315 crore and the state government will pump in the remaining Rs 285 crore. The centre will be equipped with the ProteusONE system, an advanced proton therapy technology known for its compact design and precise treatment delivery capabilities. Sarma appreciated IBA Particle Therapy India Pvt Ltd and its parent organisation, Ion Beam Applications SA of Belgium, for partnering with the state government in this endeavour. He further said that developing specialised human resources would be a key component of the project. Under the agreement, doctors, medical physicists, technicians and other essential personnel will receive specialised training from IBA. articles.title: CISF inks pact with IIT Hyderabad - Telangana Today
articles.content: NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Cisf Inks Pact With Iit Hyderabad CISF inks pact with IIT Hyderabad The CISF signed an MoU with IIT Hyderabad's TiHAN to strengthen its preparedness against drone and aerial threats. The collaboration will provide specialised drone training to personnel and technical support for a proposed Centre of Excellence in Rajasthan By Telangana Today Published Date - 1 November 2026, 10:30 AM Hyderabad: In a move to strengthen its long-term operational preparedness against asymmetric aerial threats, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with TiHAN (Technology Innovation Hub on Autonomous Navigation) at the Indian I nstitute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad. Under the ambit of the collaboration, Assistant Commandant probationers and Sub-Inspector trainees at NISA will undergo specialised short-duration capsule courses at TiHAN. Trainees will gain hands-on exposure to drone assembly, flight operations, and advanced autonomous systems research in TiHAN’s laboratories. Furthermore, TiHAN will provide essential academic and technical support to the CISF’s upcoming Centre of Excellence for Drone and Anti-Drone Technology at the Recruit Training Centre (RTC) in Behror, Rajasthan. Elaborating on the strategic objectives of the collaboration, NISA Director and IG Harpreet Kaur Sohi said this MoU would significantly increase specialisation within the force, directly supporting newly formed functional sector pattern of supervision. “By embedding advanced academic research into our training frameworks, we are creating a dynamic, knowledge-based ecosystem in the CISF. This ensures our personnel are not just guarding vital assets, but are equipped with the intelligence-led, technical expertise required to anticipate and neutralise future threats,” said Sohi. TiHAN Project Director Prof. Rajlakshmi P noted that this agreement would translate TiHAN’s advanced autonomous research into everyday operational utility for the CISF, directly advancing the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision in critical security technologies.
